package_info.package_versions: Electron Windows and Mac desktop app versions distributed in March 2023 (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CX Desktop App was compromised via a supply chain attack, where threat actors inserted malicious code into the official software update. This code enabled remote command execution and malware installation on user systems, turning a trusted software update into a vector for widespread compromise.

execution_context.file_location: Electron app bundle (main process JavaScript file, e.g., main.js or a loaded module)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime (upon app launch or update), the code downloads a secondary payload from a remote server, writes it to disk, and executes it, enabling remote code execution and further malware installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes a binary from an external, non-3CX domain, which is a classic indicator of a supply chain compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal update or app code should not fetch and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet, especially from non-official domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may download signed updates from official servers, but never execute unsigned or unverified code from third-party domains.
key_indicators: Writing and executing a new binary at runtime
Lack of code signature or verification for downloaded payload

attack_chain.action: Threat actors compromise the Trading Technologies software supply chain, gaining access to 3CX build environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Insertion of malicious code into 3CX app update

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the 3CX Electron app and distributed via official update channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code on user systems

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or launch, the malicious code in the 3CX app downloads and executes a secondary payload from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and further malware deployment

attack_chain.action: Secondary payload enables threat actors to execute arbitrary commands, steal data, or install additional malware.

behavioral_signatures: Electron app making network requests to non-official domains at runtime
Unexpected file writes and process execution by desktop app
App update process resulting in new, unsigned binaries being executed
file_indicators: Electron app main process files (main.js, preload.js) containing fetch or network code to unknown domains
Unexpected binaries (e.g., payload.exe) appearing in app directories after update
network_indicators: Outbound connections from 3CX app to domains not owned by 3CX (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
Unusual download of executable content during or after app update
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Electron-based applications for unexpected network requests to non-official domains, especially during or after updates. Inspect app code for injected fetch or download logic. Alert on new executable files written and launched by the app process. Correlate update events with subsequent process creation and network activity to detect supply chain compromise.
